racePreview.title: Monaco GP
racePreview.headline: Ferrari's big chance as FIA neuters Mercedes power advantage
racePreview.summary: Antonelli leads Russell by 43 points after four straight wins, but Monaco's tight corners and no Straight Mode zones could finally hand Ferrari their first victory of 2026.
racePreview.body:
Kimi Antonelli has won four races in a row now — including a dramatic Canadian GP where he and George Russell were scrapping hard for the lead before Russell's power unit gave up on Lap 30. That's extended Antonelli's championship lead to 43 points, and the kid's only 19. Russell bounced back in Canada by taking pole for both the Sprint and Grand Prix — beating Antonelli by exactly 0.068s each time — and won the Sprint, but the main race went south when the mechanical gremlins hit. McLaren meanwhile are looking to rebound after a costly strategic misstep in Canada that left them off the podium despite having the pace. Mercedes have won every Grand Prix this season but that streak's under serious threat here.

Ferrari's car has looked very strong in corners but lacking on straights, whereas Mercedes will potentially lose some of its power advantage in Monaco. Even better for Ferrari — the FIA has confirmed there will be no Straight Mode zones at Monaco this weekend, with both wings staying in high-downforce configuration throughout for safety reasons. Ferrari continued their strong start with Lewis Hamilton topping FP2 from Charles Leclerc, and qualifying on Saturday is absolutely everything here because overtaking is nearly impossible. Leclerc could well take his fourth pole in Monaco, while Hamilton will be buoyed by a best-ever finish in red, with second last time out in Canada. If either Ferrari nails it on Saturday, don't be surprised if Mercedes finally drop their first Grand Prix of 2026.

raceRecap.title: Monaco GP
raceRecap.headline: Antonelli untouchable in Monaco as penalties wreck Russell's race
raceRecap.summary: Kimi Antonelli made it five wins in a row at Monaco while teammate George Russell scored zero after a pitlane penalty disaster dropped him 68 points behind in the championship.
raceRecap.body:
Verstappen's race ended before it began — the Red Bull lost power on the formation lap and he couldn't even get off the grid, all 21 cars streaming past him before he rolled into retirement. Antonelli was left alone out front from pole and never looked back, building a gap over Hamilton and Leclerc behind while chaos unfolded everywhere else. Norris retired with power unit issues, Bottas overheated and stopped on lap 18, and then the real mess started — five drivers got handed five-second penalties for speeding in the pitlane, likely from cutting the line once they were in it. Hamilton copped one, Russell got one too and then made it worse by failing to serve it at his next stop, which earned him a drive-through penalty, and Gasly somehow managed to pick up two separate speeding penalties. The track surface broke up at the final corner with 10 laps to go, first taking out Stroll and then home hero Leclerc at the restart, triggering a red flag. Gasly crossed the line thinking he'd finished third, only to find out the 10 seconds of penalties had dropped him to seventh — he was near-disconsolate afterwards, calling it heartbreaking.

Antonelli was forced into a second restart after the red flag but stood firm against Hamilton, crossing the line 6.2 seconds clear to take his fifth consecutive win. In doing so he matched Hamilton's run of five straight wins with Mercedes, and at 19 years old became the youngest ever Monaco Grand Prix winner. Hadjar took third for his first Red Bull podium after all the penalties were sorted, with Piastri fourth as the only McLaren left running and both Racing Bulls in the points. Russell finished 12th after serving his drive-through and scored zero points, dropping him behind Hamilton in the standings. Antonelli's championship lead over Russell is now 68 points — and with his teammate having back-to-back DNFs while he's on a five-race winning streak, this title fight is starting to look like a procession.
